column1: Zoologist Ross Piper looks at the potential of insects in pharmaceutical research
column2: 动物学家罗斯·派珀探讨昆虫在药物研究中的潜力。

column1: More drugs than you might think are derived from, or inspired by, compounds found in living things.
column2: 从生物体内的化合物中获得或受其启发而研制的药物，比你想象的要多。

column1: Looking to nature for the soothing and curing of our ailments is nothing new — we have been doing it for tens of thousands of years.
column2: 向大自然寻求缓解和治疗疾病的办法并非新鲜事，人类这样做已有几万年了。
column3: Looking to nature|向大自然寻求
column7: tens of thousands of years|数万年

column1: You only have to look at other primates — such as the capuchin monkeys who rub themselves with toxin-oozing millipedes to deter mosquitoes, or the chimpanzees who use noxious forest plants to rid themselves of intestinal parasites — to realise that our ancient ancestors too probably had a basic grasp of medicine.
column2: 看看其他灵长类动物就明白了：卷尾猴会用分泌毒素的马陆擦身以驱赶蚊虫，黑猩猩则利用有毒的森林植物驱除肠道寄生虫。由此不难想到，远古人类可能也掌握了基本的医药知识。

column1: Pharmaceutical science and chemistry built on these ancient foundations and perfected the extraction, characterisation, modification and testing of these natural products.
column2: 药物科学和化学在这些古老经验的基础上发展起来，并完善了提取、鉴定、改造和检验这些天然产物的方法。

column1: Then, for a while, modern pharmaceutical science moved its focus away from nature and into the laboratory, designing chemical compounds from scratch.
column2: 此后有一段时间，现代药物科学把重点从自然界转到实验室，开始从零设计化合物。
column4: moved its focus|转移了研究重点

column1: The main cause of this shift is that although there are plenty of promising chemical compounds in nature, finding them is far from easy.
column2: 这次转变的主要原因是，自然界虽然有大量前景可观的化合物，找到它们却远非易事。

column1: Securing sufficient numbers of the organism in question, isolating and characterising the compounds of interest, and producing large quantities of these compounds are all significant hurdles.
column2: 要获取足够数量的目标生物、分离并鉴定感兴趣的化合物、再把这些化合物大量制备出来，每一步都有很大的难度。
column5: organism in question|所研究的生物
column8: compounds of interest|所关注的化合物

column1: Laboratory-based drug discovery has achieved varying levels of success, something which has now prompted the development of new approaches focusing once again on natural products.
column2: 依靠实验室发现新药取得的成效不一，这促使研究者开发新方法，再次把目光投向天然产物。
column5: varying levels of success|程度不一的成效

column1: With the ability to mine genomes for useful compounds, it is now evident that we have barely scratched the surface of nature’s molecular diversity.
column2: 如今有了从基因组中发掘有用化合物的能力，我们愈发清楚：对于自然界分子层面的多样性，我们至今只触及皮毛。
column7: barely scratched the surface of|才刚触及……的皮毛

column1: This realisation, together with several looming health crises, such as antibiotic resistance, has put bioprospecting — the search for useful compounds in nature — firmly back on the map.
column2: 认识到这一点，再加上抗生素耐药等几种迫近的健康危机，人们重新开始重视生物勘探，也就是从自然界中寻找有用的化合物。
column8: back on the map|重新受到重视

column1: Insects are the undisputed masters of the terrestrial domain, where they occupy every possible niche.
column2: 昆虫无疑是陆地上的主宰，几乎每一种可能的生态位里都能找到它们。

column1: Consequently, they have a bewildering array of interactions with other organisms, something which has driven the evolution of an enormous range of very interesting compounds for defensive and offensive purposes.
column2: 因此，昆虫与其他生物之间有着极其繁杂的相互作用，这促使它们在进化中形成种类繁多、十分有意思的化合物，用于防御或攻击。
column4: bewildering array|令人眼花缭乱的多种多样的事物

column1: Their remarkable diversity exceeds that of every other group of animals on the planet combined.
column2: 昆虫的多样性惊人，超过地球上其他所有动物类群加起来的多样性。

column1: Yet even though insects are far and away the most diverse animals in existence, their potential as sources of therapeutic compounds is yet to be realised.
column2: 昆虫的多样性虽然远超其他现存动物，但作为治疗性化合物的来源，其潜力尚待发掘。
column8: yet to be realised|尚待实现

column1: From the tiny proportion of insects that have been investigated, several promising compounds have been identified.
column2: 迄今接受研究的昆虫只占极小一部分，但研究者已从中发现了几种有前景的化合物。

column1: For example, alloferon, an antimicrobial compound produced by blow fly larvae, is used as an antiviral and antitumor agent in South Korea and Russia.
column2: 例如，丽蝇幼虫产生的抗微生物物质阿洛菲隆，已在韩国和俄罗斯用作抗病毒和抗肿瘤药剂。

column1: The larvae of a few other insect species are being investigated for the potent antimicrobial compounds they produce.
column2: 研究者还在考察另外几种昆虫的幼虫，因为它们能产生效力很强的抗微生物化合物。

column1: Meanwhile, a compound from the venom of the wasp Polybia paulista has potential in cancer treatment.
column2: 与此同时，人们发现，学名为Polybia paulista的一种胡蜂，其毒液里有一种化合物有望用于治疗癌症。

column1: Why is it that insects have received relatively little attention in bioprospecting?
column2: 为什么昆虫在生物勘探中受到的关注相对较少？
column4: relatively little attention|相对较少的关注

column1: Firstly, there are so many insects that, without some manner of targeted approach, investigating this huge variety of species is a daunting task.
column2: 首先，昆虫实在太多了。如果没有某种有针对性的方法，研究数量如此庞大的物种是一项令人生畏的任务。
column6: huge variety of species|种类繁多的物种

column1: Secondly, insects are generally very small, and the glands inside them that secrete potentially useful compounds are smaller still.
column2: 其次，昆虫通常很小，而虫体内分泌潜在有用化合物的腺体就更小了。

column1: This can make it difficult to obtain sufficient quantities of the compound for subsequent testing.
column2: 因此，要取得足量化合物来做后续测试并不容易。

column1: Thirdly, although we consider insects to be everywhere, the reality of this ubiquity is vast numbers of a few extremely common species.
column2: 第三，我们固然觉得昆虫无处不在，但这种“无处不在”的实情是：少数极常见的物种有着极其庞大的个体数量。

column1: Many insect species are infrequently encountered and very difficult to rear in captivity, which, again, can leave us with insufficient material to work with.
column2: 许多昆虫很少能遇到，人工饲养也非常困难，因此研究者同样可能没有足够的材料可用。
column5: in captivity|在人工圈养条件下
column6: insufficient material|不够用的研究材料

column1: My colleagues and I at Aberystwyth University in the UK have developed an approach in which we use our knowledge of ecology as a guide to target our efforts.
column2: 我和英国阿伯里斯特威斯大学的同事们开发了一种方法，用生态学知识作指引，帮助我们确定研究的目标。
column4: developed an approach|提出了一种方法
column7: target our efforts|确定投入研究的方向

column1: The creatures that particularly interest us are the many insects that secrete powerful poison for subduing prey and keeping it fresh for future consumption.
column2: 我们特别感兴趣的是这样一大类昆虫：它们分泌强效毒液制伏猎物，并使猎物保持新鲜，留待日后食用。
column7: keeping it fresh|使猎物保持新鲜

column1: There are even more insects that are masters of exploiting filthy habitats, such as faeces and carcasses, where they are regularly challenged by thousands of micro-organisms.
column2: 还有更多昆虫善于利用肮脏的生境，例如粪便和动物尸体。在那里，它们经常要面对成千上万种微生物的挑战。

column1: These insects have many antimicrobial compounds for dealing with pathogenic bacteria and fungi, suggesting that there is certainly potential to find many compounds that can serve as or inspire new antibiotics.
column2: 这些昆虫拥有许多抗微生物化合物，能够对付致病细菌和真菌。这表明，无论直接寻找可作新型抗生素的化合物，还是从中得到新药开发的启发，都大有可为。

column1: Although natural history knowledge points us in the right direction, it doesn’t solve the problems associated with obtaining useful compounds from insects.
column2: 自然史知识虽然为我们指明了方向，但并没有解决如何从昆虫中获得有用化合物的问题。
column4: points us in the right direction|为我们指明方向

column1: Fortunately, it is now possible to snip out the stretches of the insect’s DNA that carry the codes for the interesting compounds and insert them into cell lines that allow larger quantities to be produced.
column2: 好在如今已经可以取出昆虫DNA中为所关注化合物编码的片段，将其导入细胞系，从而生产出更多这些化合物。
column5: carry the codes for|携带为……编码的信息

column1: And although the road from isolating and characterising compounds with desirable qualities to developing a commercial product is very long and full of pitfalls, the variety of successful animal-derived pharmaceuticals on the market demonstrates there is a precedent here that is worth exploring.
column2: 从分离、鉴定具备所需特性的化合物，到将其开发成商品，这条路虽然漫长而且处处可能遇到难关，但市场上已有多种成功的动物来源药物，可见这条路有先例可循，值得探索。

column1: With every bit of wilderness that disappears, we deprive ourselves of potential medicines.
column2: 每消失一片荒野，我们就让自己少了一些找到新药的机会。
column6: deprive ourselves of|使我们自己失去
column7: potential medicines|可能被发现的药物

column1: As much as I’d love to help develop a groundbreaking insect-derived medicine, my main motivation for looking at insects in this way is conservation.
column2: 我固然很想参与研制一种源于昆虫、具有突破性意义的药物，但以这种方式研究昆虫，我最主要的动机还是保护它们。

column1: I sincerely believe that all species, however small and seemingly insignificant, have a right to exist for their own sake.
column2: 我由衷地相信，一切物种，无论多么微小、看起来多么不起眼，都有单凭其自身价值而存在的权利。
column8: for their own sake|仅凭它们自身的价值

column1: If we can shine a light on the darker recesses of nature’s medicine cabinet, exploring the useful chemistry of the most diverse animals on the planet, I believe we can make people think differently about the value of nature.
column2: 大自然像一只药柜。如果我们能照亮其中鲜为人知的角落，探究地球上种类最丰富的这些动物身上有何有用的化学物质，我相信，人们会重新思考大自然的价值。
column3: shine a light on|使人们关注并了解
column8: the value of nature|大自然的价值
